variants.title: A · Decision card
variants.specific: Layout A: ONE focused, elegant decision card, centered in the main content area, about 890px wide, softly bordered white card with a narrow teal top accent. The card has a clear vertical sequence with generous spacing. At top small Needs review and source context; then large headline. Three horizontal facts as lightweight text groups separated by fine vertical lines, NOT many cards. A single pale teal recommendation area: Buy 8 pallets large on the left, €1,420 estimated aligned right, short explanation below. Next step is one simple line below recommendation. Alternatives are a single closed disclosure row; show the tiny conditional/too-late option labels beside it. Keep why/sources/ask links quiet in the card footer. Primary Review plan aligned bottom right with Revise beside it. Do not fill the entire viewport with widgets. Large breathing room around this one card. Visible variant tag exactly "A · Decision card".
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one polished desktop AdaptOps screenshot, 1536 x 1024 landscape.
Reference image is a STYLE and COMPANY-SCENARIO reference only. The user explicitly wants much LEANER information with far less copy, fewer boxes and more whitespace. Preserve the established white and very pale blue background, dark navy text, teal accents, fine borders, outline icons, familiar wordmark and enterprise UI. English only. Do NOT reproduce the dense previous screen. No photos or decoration. No browser frame or 3D perspective.
Identical shell in every variant: small top bar "AdaptOps" | "Demo Materials", right "Paul"; left navigation about 205px wide with Overview, Watchtower (selected pale teal), Actions, Company, Data & Connections. Tiny top-right proposal pill containing the variant letter and title specified below. Main viewport shows the same ONE supplier event. No chat sidebar, no large evidence panel, no tables, no repeated explanations.
Content and truth constraints shared by all variants, exact concise copy:
A small pink chip "Needs review"
Page title "Secure tomorrow's delivery"
Small news context "Supplier disruption · ERP delay confirmed"
Affected item summary "Site A · Lille", "8 ISO100 pallets", "Due 23 Oct"
Recommendation label "Recommended"
Primary proposed action "Buy 8 pallets"
Cost "€1,420 estimated"
One short explanation "Protect Site B's reserved stock."
Uncertainty as a small amber dot with text "Availability to confirm"
One brief next-step line "Next: Purchasing confirms supply, then Paul reviews."
One compact alternatives disclosure "2 alternatives evaluated" with two terse items or chips "Transfer: conditional" and "Wait: too late".
Three quiet secondary disclosure links "Why this plan?", "Sources (3)", "Ask AdaptOps" accessible on demand, not open.
ONE primary teal button "Review plan". One subtle text link "Revise".
Footer small but readable "Design proposal · Synthetic data · Controlled scenario"
The financial number is a proposed cost, never savings. No execution has happened. Purchasing must confirm availability before approval. Never show a completed purchase, live feed badge or invented success. No additional content. Use a comfortably readable 16-18px body text equivalent, generous white space, one-line summaries. All essential content fits without scrolling. No em dashes.

variants.title: B · Three-step brief
variants.specific: Layout B: A clean horizontal briefing story across the main canvas. No giant enclosing card. Page title top-left with small source line and needs-review chip. Beneath, three equal airy columns in ONE row, joined only by delicate small arrows and separated by whitespace. Column 1 has a tiny "01 / News" eyebrow, simple document icon, short supplier/ERP context. Column 2 has "02 / Impact", location icon, and large "8 pallets" followed by ISO100, Site A · Lille, Due 23 Oct. Column 3 has "03 / Response", pale teal background ONLY behind this recommended response column, Buy 8 pallets, €1,420 estimated, Protect Site B's reserved stock, Availability to confirm. A narrow line beneath the three columns carries Next: Purchasing confirms supply, then Paul reviews. Below it compact collapsed alternatives row with both terse option evaluations. The lower portion contains a single prominent Review plan button to the right and quiet disclosure links to the left. Keep the main canvas lightweight, 60 percent whitespace, large readable type. Visible variant tag exactly "B · Three-step brief". Use each fact once; do not repeat the source line in multiple places.

variants.title: C · Plan first
variants.specific: Layout C: A two-column layout in the main canvas, around 42 percent left and 58 percent right, with generous whitespace. Title across top. Left is an unboxed crisp editorial incident summary with small Needs review chip, supplier/ERP one-line news, a thin rule, then Site A · Lille, 8 ISO100 pallets, Due 23 Oct in a very short vertical list. Beneath those facts, a compact collapsed alternatives disclosure showing Transfer: conditional and Wait: too late in muted text. RIGHT is a larger pale teal panel with the prepared response as the visual focal point: small Recommended eyebrow, very large Buy 8 pallets, €1,420 estimated, one sentence Protect Site B's reserved stock, amber dot Availability to confirm. A thin divider then the one-line next step. Wide primary Review plan button within this right panel, small Revise link below. Along the bottom edge of main canvas sit quiet Why this plan?, Sources (3), Ask AdaptOps links. This must feel markedly different from A's single central card and B's horizontal story, while showing exactly the same information. Visible variant tag exactly "C · Plan first".
